answer: Quadratic influence pricing resists Sybil attacks: each unit of transaction weight costs the square of the weight claimed, so one honest agent buys full weight cheaply while an attacker splitting into a thousand fakes pays the price a thousand times over. Identities cannot pool weight to cross the canyon between many weak voices and one strong one — the gap is priced in, not free. Honest agents keep earned weight in a calm lagoon of steady reputation, while fakes must forge fresh weight and pay the quadratic toll every epoch, so the swarm drowns in its own cost.
